hints: Substitute $x = 1$ into $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{6}{(3x - 2)^3}$ to find the gradient $\frac{dy}{dx} = 6$.
Apply the chain rule for rates of change: $\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{dy/dt}{dy/dx}$ with $\frac{dy}{dt} = 3\text{ units/s}$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the derivative at the point $A(1, -3)$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1} = \frac{6}{(3(1) - 2)^3} = \frac{6}{1^3} = 6$$

Apply the chain rule for connected rates of change:
$$\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{\frac{dy}{dt}}{\frac{dy}{dx}} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ unit per second}$$

hints: Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 6(3x - 2)^{-3}$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule: $\frac{6(3x - 2)^{-2}}{-2 \times 3} + c = -(3x - 2)^{-2} + c$.
Substitute point $A(1, -3)$ into the integrated equation to determine the constant of integration $c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative using the power and chain rules:
$$y = \int 6(3x - 2)^{-3} dx = \frac{6(3x - 2)^{-2}}{-2 \times 3} + c = -(3x - 2)^{-2} + c = -\frac{1}{(3x - 2)^2} + c$$

Substitute the coordinates of point $A(1, -3)$ into the equation to find $c$:
$$-3 = -\frac{1}{(3(1) - 2)^2} + c = -1 + c \implies c = -3 + 1 = -2$$

Write down the complete curve equation:
$$y = -(3x - 2)^{-2} - 2 \quad \left(\text{or } y = -\frac{1}{(3x - 2)^2} - 2\right)$$
